ios.desc:
Builderment is a factory building game at heart. It’s all about crafting and automation. You start by harvesting resources and crafting items in factories. Use those crafted items to research new technology and recipes to craft ever more complex items.

Earth has run out of resources... You have been sent to a distant planet to extract its infinite resources and craft items to send back to Earth. You'll need to establish a base on this planet to build factories and production lines to automate the assembly of items.

Features
* Build factories on a massive scale
* Use conveyor belts to transport items between factories
* Craft dozens of unique items
* Research technology to build more advanced buildings
* Expand to harvest every resource on the map

quotes.text:
> How on earth are you going to clone a game like Stardew Valley, or Disco Elysium, or Factorio, or No Man's Sky, or Subnautica

Stardew Valley clones: https://gamerant.com/stardew-valley-clone-harvest-life-super-zoo-story/

Factorio has a bunch of games that if not clones, are pretty damn similar to Factorio. I'm playing one right now called Dyson Sphere Program, but there's Satisfactory, Mindustry, Automation Empire, Shapez.io, FactoryIdle.com, and here's one on iOS in particular (since we're talking about mobile games) called Builderment: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/builderment/id1558592038

Subnautica: https://forums.unknownworlds.com/discussion/141925/subnautica-copycats
Hell, people claiming No Man's Sky's new content update being heavily inspired by Subnautica: https://forums.unknownworlds.com/discussion/155102/no-mans-sky-stealing-from-subnautica

No Man's Sky already has a bunch of similar games that predates it on a bit smaller scale, but here's one I found that looks heavily inspired by it: https://steamcommunity.com/app/275850/discussions/0/412446292757297621/?l=polish&ctp=1

Disco Elysium is so heavily narrative driven it's not a good candidate for a clone, sure, and also it's not the sort of game that would appeal to a casual app crowd, so it's not a good candidate for being cloned anyway. I guess you found one!

I'm not saying there's nothing out there that can't be cloned, obviously a couple of guys at a clone studio aren't going to crank out a game in a …
quotes.story_title: Clone culture and its continuous impact on indie developers
